mission.progress_signals.v1:
## Runtime Signals
If you emit Armada signals, print each signal on its own standalone line with no bullets, quoting, or extra Markdown:
- `[ARMADA:PROGRESS] 50` -- report completion percentage (0-100)
- `[ARMADA:STATUS] Testing` -- report that you are now running tests (informational; `[ARMADA:STATUS] InProgress` switches back)
- `[ARMADA:MESSAGE] your message here` -- send a progress message
- `[ARMADA:TOKENS] input=1234 output=567 cached=0` -- report the tokens you consumed this session (input/prompt, output/completion, and cache-read). Emit this once near the end if your runtime can determine the counts; it lets the Admiral record real token usage instead of an estimate.
- `[ARMADA:RESULT] COMPLETE` -- worker/test engineer mission finished successfully
- `[ARMADA:STAGE-OUTCOME] BLOCKED` -- any persona: you cannot proceed because of an external prerequisite (for example work another mission has not landed yet) or a contradictory brief. End with this standalone line instead of a result or verdict line, followed by one paragraph giving the reason; do not change files for work you cannot do. Verifier stages that found a product defect use the same line with an `## Affected Case` section.
- `[ARMADA:VERDICT] PASS` -- judge approves the mission
- `[ARMADA:VERDICT] FAIL` -- judge rejects the mission
- `[ARMADA:VERDICT] NEEDS_REVISION` -- judge requests follow-up changes
Architect missions must not emit `[ARMADA:RESULT]` or `[ARMADA:VERDICT]`; they must output only real mission definitions: one fenced `armada-plan` JSON block (preferred) or real `[ARMADA:MISSION]` blocks.
